knowledge:
- key_parameters: condition=The column name in the spatial object representing the experimental condition or "survival" for survival analysis ;; from=The starting cell type for testing a specific pairwise localization ;; to=The target cell type for testing a specific pairwise localization ;; cellType=The column name containing cell type annotations (defaults to "cellType") ;; alternateResult=A data frame or matrix of custom distance or abundance metrics to use instead of the default L-function ;; weights=Logical, whether to use weights in the linear model (set to FALSE when using alternateResult) ;; subject=The column name representing the subject/random effect for mixed-effects modeling ;; sigma=The bandwidth parameter for kernel density estimation to account for tissue inhomogeneity (defaults to NULL for homogeneous structure) ;; Rs=The distance range/radius for calculating pairwise associations in getPairwise
- alternatives: imcRtools::buildSpatialGraph=Used to construct kNN interaction graphs which can be converted to custom abundance metrics ;; Statial=Mentioned as a package containing other custom distance metrics that can be used with spicyR
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have multi-image, single-cell resolution spatial omics data (e.g., multiplexed ion beam imaging, imaging mass cytometry) and want to statistically evaluate if the spatial co-localization or dispersion of cell type pairs significantly differs across clinical conditions, patient groups, or is associated with patient survival.
- pitfalls: S4 Method Dispatch Bug=SingleCellExperiment and SpatialExperiment objects may not correctly inherit from SummarizedExperiment. A workaround class union must be defined before running the analysis ;; Tissue Inhomogeneity=Dense cell clustering (e.g., tumor nests) can cause false-positive attraction signals. Use the sigma parameter in spicy() or getPairwise() to correct for this ;; Survival Column Requirement=For survival analysis, the input object must contain a column named exactly "survival" containing a Surv object.

workflows.name: pairwise_localization_modeling
workflows.intent: Test for changes in pairwise cell type localization across conditions using linear or mixed-effects models.
input: kerenSPE (SpatialExperiment object containing single-cell spatial coordinates, cell type annotations, and condition metadata)
diabetesData (SpatialExperiment object containing multi-image data per subject for mixed-effects modeling)
workflows.stages: 1. Define S4 class union workaround for the inheritance bug ;; 2. Run spicy() for a specific cell pair or all pairwise combinations ;; 3. Extract coefficients and p-values using topPairs() ;; 4. Extract image-level L-function metrics using bind() ;; 5. Visualize significant relationships using signifPlot() ;; 6. Generate boxplots for specific cell-cell relationships using spicyBoxPlot() ;; 7. Perform mixed-effects modeling by specifying the subject parameter
workflows.code:
methods::setClassUnion("ExpData", c("matrix", "dgCMatrix", "ExpressionSet",
                                    "SummarizedExperiment"))

spicyTestPair <- spicy(
  kerenSPE,
  condition = "tumour_type",
  from = "CD8_T_cell",
  to = "Neutrophils"
)

topPairs(spicyTestPair)

spicyTest <- spicy(
  kerenSPE,
  condition = "tumour_type"
)

topPairs(spicyTest)

bind(spicyTest)[1:5, 1:5]

signifPlot(
  spicyTest,
  breaks = c(-3, 3, 1),
  marksToPlot = c("Macrophages", "DC_or_Mono", "dn_T_CD3", "Neutrophils",
                  "CD8_T_cell", "Keratin_Tumour")
)

spicyBoxPlot(results = spicyTest, 
             # from = "Macrophages",
             # to = "dn_T_CD3"
             rank = 1)

spicyMixedTest <- spicy(
  diabetesData,
  condition = "stage",
  subject = "case"
)

workflows.name: custom_metrics_modeling
workflows.intent: Perform spatial modeling using custom distance or abundance metrics, such as kNN interaction graphs, instead of the default L-function.
input: kerenSPE (SpatialExperiment object containing single-cell spatial coordinates and cell type annotations)
workflows.stages: 1. Build a spatial graph using imcRtools::buildSpatialGraph() ;; 2. Convert the spatial graph into an abundance matrix using convPairs() ;; 3. Run spicy() with the custom abundance matrix passed to alternateResult and weights set to FALSE ;; 4. Retrieve top pairs using topPairs() ;; 5. Visualize results using signifPlot()
workflows.code:
kerenSPE <- imcRtools::buildSpatialGraph(kerenSPE, 
                                         img_id = "imageID", 
                                         type = "knn", k = 20,
                                        coords = c("x", "y"))

pairAbundances <- convPairs(kerenSPE,
                  colPair = "knn_interaction_graph")

head(pairAbundances["B_cell__B_cell"])

spicyTestColPairs <- spicy(
  kerenSPE,
  condition = "tumour_type",
  alternateResult = pairAbundances,
  weights = FALSE
)

topPairs(spicyTestColPairs)

signifPlot(
  spicyTestColPairs,
  breaks = c(-3, 3, 1),
  marksToPlot = c("Macrophages", "dn_T_CD3", "CD4_T_cell", 
                  "B_cell", "DC_or_Mono", "Neutrophils", "CD8_T_cell")
)

workflows.name: survival_analysis
workflows.intent: Assess whether changes in co-localization between cell types are associated with patient survival probability.
input: kerenSPE (SpatialExperiment object containing survival time and censoring status columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Create a Surv object and store it in the "survival" column of the spatial object ;; 2. Run spicy() with condition set to "survival" ;; 3. Access the survival analysis results from the survivalResults slot of the output object
workflows.code:
kerenSPE$event = 1 - kerenSPE$Censored
kerenSPE$survival = Surv(kerenSPE$`Survival_days_capped*`, kerenSPE$event)

spicySurvival = spicy(kerenSPE,
                      condition = "survival")

head(spicySurvival$survivalResults, 10)

workflows.name: inhomogeneity_correction_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Account for tissue inhomogeneity in pairwise association calculations and visually inspect cellular relationships in specific images.
input: kerenSPE (SpatialExperiment object containing single-cell spatial coordinates and cell type annotations)
workflows.stages: 1. Subset the spatial object to a single image ;; 2. Calculate pairwise associations using getPairwise() without inhomogeneity correction (sigma = NULL) ;; 3. Calculate pairwise associations using getPairwise() with inhomogeneity correction (sigma = bandwidth value) ;; 4. Plot cell-cell relationships for the image using plotImage()
workflows.code:
kerenSubset = kerenSPE[, colData(kerenSPE)$imageID == "24"]

pairwiseAssoc = getPairwise(kerenSubset, 
                            sigma = NULL, 
                            Rs = 100) |>
  as.data.frame()

pairwiseAssoc[["Keratin_Tumour__Neutrophils"]]

pairwiseAssoc = getPairwise(kerenSubset, 
                            sigma = 20, 
                            Rs = 100) |>
  as.data.frame()

pairwiseAssoc[["Keratin_Tumour__Neutrophils"]]

plotImage(kerenSPE, "24", from = "Keratin_Tumour", to = "Neutrophils")
